name: Fantasy Quest
definition: A consequential charge carries travelers through a rule-bound fantastic world where trials test the values required to use, deliver, destroy, or relinquish what they seek.
negative_signals: aimless exploration without a consequential charge
diagnostic_questions: Does the objective carry moral as well as practical meaning?
Do fantastic rules alter choices and costs?

neighbors.distinction: A quest is organized by a charge and its moral burden; an expedition by exploration and discovery.
A quest may face monsters, but its promise is completion or transformation rather than sustained fear.

reader_promises.name: Worthy charge
reader_promises.description: Give the sought outcome enough personal and communal meaning to justify the journey.

reader_promises.name: Transforming trials
reader_promises.description: Make obstacles test values and relationships, not only combat capability.

roles.name: Bearer of the charge
roles.description: Carries responsibility without needing to be the strongest or most knowledgeable.

roles.name: Limited guide
roles.description: Offers access or wisdom while withholding certainty, power, or permanence.

roles.name: Quest companion
roles.description: Embodies a different need, method, or claim on the objective.

stakes: Fate of a community or order
Control or destruction of transformative power
settings: Threshold between ordinary and magical worlds

movements.name: Charge accepted
movements.description: Define the objective, fantastic rule, and cost of refusing or failing.

movements.name: Threshold crossed
movements.description: Commit to a world or rule that makes ordinary solutions insufficient.

movements.name: Value-testing trials
movements.description: Escalate through choices that reshape the party and interpretation of the charge.

movements.name: Fulfillment redefined
movements.description: Resolve the objective through an earned understanding of how or whether it should be completed.

complications.name: Price revealed
complications.description: The true cost follows an established magical or political rule.

complications.name: Companion's claim
complications.description: An ally has a legitimate incompatible need involving the objective.

complications.name: Corrupting shortcut
complications.description: A faster path would violate the value the quest supposedly protects.

twists.name: Objective's true function
twists.description: The sought thing performs a different role than tradition claimed.

twists.name: Compromised charge
twists.description: The authority that assigned the quest concealed an interest without making all purpose meaningless.

conclusions.name: Restorative return
conclusions.description: Completion changes both the world and the bearer's place within it.

conclusions.name: Renunciation
conclusions.description: The bearer protects the deeper promise by refusing the expected reward or power.

conclusions.name: New order
conclusions.description: The quest ends an inherited system and begins a less certain arrangement.

variation_axes.question: What kind of charge drives the quest?

subversions: Let the chosen bearer succeed by surrendering exceptional status.
Replace a singular evil with conflicting legitimate obligations.
cliches_to_avoid: A prophecy that removes meaningful choice
Borrowed fantasy species used as personality substitutes
quality_checks: Fantastic rules cause concrete decisions and consequences.
Trials change the meaning of the objective.
The final choice resolves the charge and the bearer's values.

sources.title: Making It Different: Pushing Genre Boundaries in Fantasy
sources.author_or_organization: Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association
sources.contribution: Argues for satisfying genre identity while challenging stock worlds, characters, and plots.

sources.title: A Checklist for Critiquing Science Fiction
sources.author_or_organization: Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association
sources.contribution: Supports consistent imagined worlds, motivated action, thematic stakes, and causal plotting.
